post.description: To rank or compare foods by a nutrient, e.g. iron (FE) across ready-to-eat breakfast cereals (sub_food_group_id 30), sodium (NA) in cheeses, or the highest-protein foods overall.

food_group_id.description:
Restrict to one AFCD food group (see list_food_groups); joins the food catalogue.

Provider reference: minimum 1.

include_food_groups.description: Fill the food group fields of every row by joining the food catalogue even without a group filter (one extra request).

nutrient_id.description: AFCD nutrient code from list_nutrients (e.g. FE, NA, PROT, ENERGY-04, 'ENERGY - AHS'); case-insensitive.

page.description:
1-based page of the client-side paginated result (the API returns the whole list).

Provider reference: minimum 1; default 1.

page_size.description:
Rows per page (1-200).

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 200; default 50.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring matched against the food name and inclusions.

sort.description:
Row order: value_desc (default), value_asc or name (AFCD alphabetical).

Provider reference: allowed values ["value_desc", "value_asc", "name"]; default "value_desc".

sub_food_group_id.description:
Restrict to one AFCD sub food group (see list_food_groups); joins the food catalogue.

Provider reference: minimum 1.

200.description:
Every AFCD food's amount of one nutrient (GET https://www.foodstandards.gov.au/science-data/food-nutrient-databases/afcd/search/api/nutrients/{nutrient_id}): the nutrient's metadata and 1,588 rows of pfk, name, inclusions and value per 100 g, which the program sorts (by value descending by default), optionally narrows with a name `query` and/or a food group / sub food group (joining the food catalogue, GET /foods/alphabetical, which also fills the group fields of each row) and pages. Rows carry the public food page URL. An unknown nutrient code is `not_found` (use list_nutrients); a filter nothing matches is an empty list.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `catalogue_size` | number | Foods AFCD reports this nutrient for before filtering. |
| `food_group_id` | number |  |
| `foods` | object[] |  |
| `nutrient` | object |  |
| `observed_at_ms` | number | Unix milliseconds when this program read the AFCD API. |
| `page` | number |  |
| `page_size` | number |  |
| `query` | string |  |
| `sort` | string |  |
| `source_url` | string | The AFCD API URL this answer was read from. |
| `sub_food_group_id` | number |  |

200.description:
The complete AFCD record of one food by Public Food Key (GET https://www.foodstandards.gov.au/science-data/food-nutrient-databases/afcd/search/api/foods/{pfk}; also accepts a pasted AFCD food page URL or a legacy afcd.foodstandards.gov.au/foodDetails.aspx?PFKID= link). Returns identity (name, description, inclusions, scientific name, AUSNUT classification, food group and sub food group), derivation and sampling notes, conversion factors, every nutrient with its raw value per 100 g, unit and the decimal places the site displays, grouped by category (Proximates, Minerals, Vitamins, Fatty acids, Amino acids, Organic acids, Other), the measurement options and the data references. Missing optional fields are null. An unknown key is `not_found`.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| --- | --- | --- |

| `classification_name` | string | Name of the AUSNUT classification; null when AFCD gives none. |
| `derivation` | string | How the nutrient profile was derived: Analysed, Borrowed, Estimated, Imputed, Label Data or Recipe. |
| `description` | string | AFCD description of the food; null when AFCD gives none. |
| `fat_factor` | number | Fatty-acid conversion factor; null when AFCD gives none. |
| `food_group` | string | AFCD food group name (e.g. 'Cereals and cereal products'). |
| `food_group_id` | number | AFCD food group id (1-22, see list_food_groups). |
| `inclusions` | string | Alternative names / included items; null when AFCD gives none. |
| `measurements` | object[] | Measurement options the AFCD site offers for scaling values. |
| `name` | string | Food name as AFCD states it. |
| `nitrogen_factor` | number | Nitrogen-to-protein conversion factor; null when AFCD gives none. |
| `nutrient_count` | number | Number of nutrient values in `nutrients`. |
| `nutrients` | object[] | Every nutrient AFCD reports for the food, in AFCD's category and display order. |
| `observed_at_ms` | number | Unix milliseconds when this program read the AFCD API. |
| `pfk` | string | Public Food Key, the AFCD food identifier (F followed by six digits, e.g. F008785 Vegemite). |
| `references` | object[] | Data sources AFCD cites for this food (may be empty). |
| `sampling_details` | string | AFCD sampling and derivation notes (which samples, which values were borrowed or imputed); null when none. |

| `specific_gravity` | number | Specific gravity (0 when not applicable); null when AFCD gives none. |
| `sub_food_group` | string | AFCD sub food group name. |
| `sub_food_group_id` | number | AFCD sub food group id (unique across groups, see list_food_groups). |
| `unanalysed_portion` | string | Share of the profile that was not analysed (e.g. '0%'); null when none. |
| `url` | string | Public AFCD food page: https://www.foodstandards.gov.au/science-data/food-nutrient-databases/afcd/search/food/{pfk}. |

categories.description: Proximates are nutrients that contribute energy to a food or beverage.
Group of organic compounds containing the carboxylic group -C(O)OH, formed by the oxidation of aldehydes. Generally analysed by chromotography.

Minerals are inorganic substances needed in the diet in small amounts to help regulate body function. From around the mid 1990's onwards, most mineral levels have been determined using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) or inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES). Before that time, atomic absorption spectroscopy was used for most mineral determination unless noted otherwise. The more recent techniques are more sensitive and therefore likely to be more reliable for minerals present in low levels.
Vitamins are organic compounds that are needed in the diet in small amounts.

Fatty acids are classified as saturated, polyunsaturated or monounsaturated depending on the presence or absence of double bonds on the carbon molecules. Saturated fatty acids contain no double bond, monounsaturated fatty acids contain one double bond per molecule, and polyunsaturated fatty acids contain more than one double bond per molecule. Polyunsaturated fatty acids can be further subdivided into those that are omega - 6 fatty acids and those that are omega - 3 fatty acids. Although all fatty acid values reported have been generated using chromatographic methods the more recent data are considered more reliable as newer techniques are better able to separate closely related fatty acids, particularly where these occur in very low levels. Fatty acids have been measured as a percentage of all extracted fatty acids and this has been converted to a mass of fatty acids using the measured fat content of the food and a conversion factor (Greenfield and Southgate, 2003: Mooney et al., 2002: Nichols, Virtue et al., 1998: Nichols, Mooney et al., 1998: Nichols et al., 2002)

Dietary amino acids are classified as essential or non-essential. Essential amino acids cannot be manufactured by the body and must be supplied in the diet. The non-essential amino acids are also essential for health, but can be synthesized in the body from the essential amino acids. Tryptophan, an essential amino acid was determined using a separate HPLC procedure or a colorimetric procedure.

nutrients.definition: Determined largely by using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS).

200.description:
Search the Australian Food Composition Database (AFCD Release 3.0, Food Standards Australia New Zealand) for foods by name (GET https://www.foodstandards.gov.au/science-data/food-nutrient-databases/afcd/search/api/foods/alphabetical, the complete catalogue of 1,588 foods, or /foods/alphabetical/{letter} when `letter` is given). AFCD has no server-side search: the program applies `query` as a case-insensitive substring match over the food name and its `inclusions` (alternative names), exactly as the AFCD site does, then filters by food group / sub food group and pages the result. Each row carries the Public Food Key (pfk) for get_food, the AUSNUT classification code, the food group pair and the public food page URL. Returns an empty `foods` list for a query nothing matches; `not_found` for a food_group_id / sub_food_group_id that does not exist in AFCD or a page past the last one.

features: SOM VIBRANTE E POTENTE - Experimente um áudio aprimorado — vocais mais nítidos, graves mais potentes — para uma experiência Echo Dot ainda mais imersiva.
SUAS MÚSICAS E CONTEÚDOS FAVORITOS - Reproduza músicas e podcasts do Amazon Music, Apple Music, Spotify, entre outros, ou por Bluetooth em todos os ambientes da sua casa.

SEMPRE DISPONÍVEL PARA AJUDAR - Pergunte a previsão do tempo para Alexa, defina timers com sua voz, obtenha respostas e ouça piadas. Precisa de mais uns minutinhos de sono pela manhã? É só tocar no seu Echo Dot para adiar o alarme.

MAIS CONFORTO EM CASA - Controle dispositivos de casa inteligente compatíveis por voz ou com rotinas ativadas por sensores de temperatura internos. Crie rotinas para ligar o ar condicionado se a temperatura interna estiver mais quente que o ideal.

DESENVOLVIDO PARA PROTEGER A SUA PRIVACIDADE - A Amazon não vende informações pessoais de clientes. O Echo Dot foi construído com várias camadas de controles de privacidade, incluindo o botão de desligar o microfone.
APROVEITE AO MÁXIMO O PAREAMENTO DE DISPOSITIVOS - Escute música na casa toda usando os dispositivos Echo compatíveis em cômodos diferentes ou crie um sistema de home theater com o Fire TV.

specifications.name: Peso
specifications.value: 304 gramas. O tamanho e o peso reais podem variar de acordo com o processo de fabricação.

specifications.name: Conectividade wifi
specifications.value: Wifi de banda dupla suporta redes 802.11 a/b/g/n/ac (2,4 e 5 GHz). Incompatível com a conexão a redes wifi ad-hoc (ou ponto a ponto).

specifications.name: Compatibilidade com dispositivos de Casa Inteligente
specifications.value: Wifi, Bluetooth Low Energy e Matter.

specifications.name: Conectividade Bluetooth
specifications.value: Oferece suporte ao Perfil de distribuição de áudio avançada (A2DP) para streaming de áudio do seu dispositivo móvel para o Echo Dot ou do Echo Dot para o seu alto-falante Bluetooth. Perfil de controle remoto de áudio/vídeo (AVRCP) para controle de voz de dispositivos móveis conectados. O controle por voz no modo de mãos livres não é compatível com dispositivos Mac OS X. Os alto-falantes Bluetooth que exigem códigos PIN não são compatíveis.

specifications.name: Requisitos do sistema
specifications.value: O Echo Dot vem pronto para se conectar à rede wifi. O aplicativo Alexa é compatível com dispositivos Fire OS, Android e iOS. A lista de sistemas operacionais compatíveis pode ser encontrada aqui. Determinadas Skills e serviços podem exigir taxas de inscrição ou outros tipos de taxa.

specifications.name: Tecnologia de configuração
specifications.value: A configuração simples de wifi da Amazon permite que clientes conectem dispositivos inteligentes à rede wifi em poucas etapas fáceis. A configuração simples de wifi é outra maneira pela qual Alexa se torna cada vez mais inteligente. Saiba mais.

specifications.name: Garantia
specifications.value: Garantia limitada por 1 ano inclusa. O uso do Echo está sujeito aos termos encontrados aqui.

specifications.name: Recursos de acessibilidade
specifications.value: O aplicativo Alexa e os produtos habilitados para Alexa incluem vários recursos para clientes com necessidades de acessibilidade relacionadas à visão, audição, mobilidade e fala. Saiba mais sobre a acessibilidade de Alexa.

specifications.name: Inclusos na caixa
specifications.value: Echo Dot 5ª geração, adaptador de energia bivolt na cor branca (15W) e Guia de início rápido

specifications.name: Recursos de privacidade
specifications.value: Tecnologia de palavra de ativação, indicadores de streaming, botão de desligamento do microfone, capacidade de visualizar e excluir suas gravações de voz e muito mais. Visite o Portal de privacidade de Alexa para explorar como Alexa e os dispositivos Echo são desenvolvidos para proteger sua privacidade.

specifications.name: Skills e recursos de Alexa
specifications.value: Alexa torna sua vida mais fácil, significativa e divertida ao permitir que a sua voz controle seu mundo. Alexa ajuda você a aproveitar mais ainda as coisas que já ama e descobrir novas possibilidades inimagináveis. Descubra e saiba tudo o que Alexa pode fazer. Você pode encontrar anúncios em dispositivos Echo e Alexa.

specifications.name: Atualizações de segurança de software
specifications.value: Este dispositivo recebe atualizações de segurança de software garantidas até pelo menos quatro anos após o dispositivo estar disponível pela última vez para compra como uma nova unidade em nossos sites. Saiba mais sobre essas atualizações de segurança de software. Se você já possui um Amazon Echo, acesse a página Gerencie seu conteúdo e dispositivos para obter informações específicas do seu dispositivo.

200.description:
Full current list of one BEA county table for one state (or the United States and its eight BEA regions with state US), paginated with a cursor pinned to the table's publication_id. Page 1 fetches the state total row(s) and the state's county list, then the first chunk of counties; each later page fetches one chunk. Segment key: (table, state, line_code, years). Every page re-reads the 'Last updated' note and fails with invalid_input code publication_changed when it differs from the pinned vintage, so two vintages are never mixed. With line_code the page holds one statistic; without it every line of the table. years accepts ALL, LAST<n> (resolved against the table's year list), one year or a comma list. Values keep BEA's flags ((D) suppressed, (NA) not available, (NM), (L), (T)) in data_value with value null.

value.text:
October 9, 2026 Decision 30958-D01-2026

Kneehill Solar GP Inc.
2930, 155 Wellington Street West
Toronto, Ont. M5V 3H1

Attention: Yasser Beshr

Kneehill Energy Storage Facility Letter of Enquiry
Proceeding 30958
Application 30958-A001

Approval of minor amendments

1. Kneehill Solar GP Inc., by Application 30958-A001, registered on July 21, 2026, applied
to the Alberta Utilities Commission for approval to make minor amendments to the 10-megawatt
(MW) energy storage facility within the existing Kneehill Solar Generation Facility boundary, in
the Three Hills area.

2. The proposed work is related to facilities previously approved by the Commission but not
yet constructed in Approval 30539-D02-2026.
1

3. Kneehill Solar requested to update the equipment of the battery energy storage system
from the SolBank system to the HyperBlock system, a type of HyperStrong system.
Kneehill Solar indicated that the number of containers would be reduced from eight to five,
inverters would be reduced from eight to three, and transformers would be reduced from four to
three. Kneehill Solar confirmed that the HyperBlock system uses the same lithium iron
phosphate battery chemistry as the approved configuration and that the proposed changes are not
changing the battery technology or associated characteristics.
2

4. Kneehill Solar confirmed that the project capability remains the same as what was
approved, at 10 MW/20 megawatt-hours.

5. Kneehill Solar stated that the proposed HyperBlock system incorporates safety systems
and design features that are comparable to the approved SolBank system and are intended to
prevent, detect and mitigate thermal events, fire hazards and explosion risks. Kneehill Solar
confirmed that it will continue to meet the safety obligations in the approval, including energy
storage facility-related training, ongoing safety upgrades and annual updates to the site-specific
emergency response plan.

1
 Energy Storage Facility Approval 30539-D02-2026, Proceeding 30539, Application 30539-A001,
January 28, 2026.
2
 Exhibit 30958-X0001, Letter of Enquiry for Minor Amendment, PDF page 2. Alberta Utilities Commission
October 9, 2026  Page 2 of 2

6. Kneehill Solar provided a letter from Stantec Consulting Ltd., which confirmed that the
original dispersion modelling and risk assessment prepared by Calvin Consulting Group Ltd. for
the approved battery system remains valid and that the carbon monoxide release rates observed
during HyperBlock testing are below the carbon monoxide emission rate used in the original
modelling assessment.
3
 Kneehill Solar confirmed that the proposed HyperBlock system would
not be expected to result in materially different hydrogen fluoride emissions or hydrogen
fluoride-related risk outcomes than the system evaluated in the original assessment.
4

7. Kneehill Solar retained Green Cat Renewables Canada Corporation to complete a noise
impact assessment for the proposed equipment which concluded that the project will comply
with Rule 012: Noise Control.
5

8. Kneehill Solar confirmed that the proposed changes are limited to internal equipment
arrangement to be located within the approved project boundary.

9. Kneehill Solar has provided information respecting the need, nature, extent, land
affected, land ownership and the timing of the work. Kneehill Solar also stated that no adverse
environmental impact will be caused by the proposed work.

10. Based upon the information provided, the Commission is satisfied that the proposed
amendment to the energy storage facility is of a minor nature, no person is directly and adversely
affected by the proposal, and no significant adverse environmental impact will be caused by the
proposed work. The Commission approves the amendment to the energy storage facility.

11. Approval 30958-D02-2026 is attached.

12. The Commission may, no later than 60 days from the date of this decision and without
notice, correct typographical, spelling and calculation errors and other similar types of errors and
post the corrected decision on its website.

Alberta Utilities Commission

Rita Chan
Director – Power Plants, Facilities Division
On behalf of the Alberta Utilities Commission

Attachment

3

4
 Exhibit 30958-X0018, KneehillSolar-Response_to_AUC_Information_Request_Round_2.
5
 Exhibit 30958-X0015, Attachment 3 - Kneehill BESS - LOE NIA Letter.

Proceeding 30732 Register

Decision 30732-D01-2026
AUC contact: Victor Choy
403-592-4439 or victor.choy@auc.ab.ca
Synapse Real Estate Corp: Jason Van Gaal
613-797-3311 or jason@synapsedatacenter.com
Overview
Synapse Real Estate Corp applied to construct and operate a combined-cycle natural gas-fired power plant with a nominal capacity of approximately 1,400 megawatts (MW) as well as 1,800 MW of emergency and backup diesel generation (the power plant). The application stated that the power plant will not be connected to the Alberta Interconnection Electric System but will be used to power the on-site data centre load. The application was filed under the Hydro and Electric Energy Act.
On August 17, 2026, the AUC denied the Synapse Data Center Power Plant Project application. The Commission finds that the project is too close to the surrounding community, and Synapse failed to demonstrate any compelling justification for selecting that location. The site is simply not suitable for the proposed development. In making this finding, the Commission is not commenting on the suitability of a data centre in this location. The Commission does not approve or regulate data centres.
Hearing information
To learn more about the review process, or for more information about how you may become involved in this proceeding, please contact us or visit the following webpages:

The eFiling System​
The eFiling System should be accessed to view the applications and the other documents the AUC will be considering in this proceeding. The system is also used to file submissions and evidence to participate in the proceeding.
To create an account, select “New account” and follow the steps to create a user ID and password. If you have any questions about how to use the eFiling System please contact us at info@auc.ab.ca or 310-4AUC.

200.description:
The Bank of Canada policy interest rate (target for the overnight rate, Valet series V39079): the rate in effect today or on any date since 1992, the most recent change and every change in the history window (three years back by default), each with the previous rate and the move in basis points. A decision the series has not yet published (it takes effect the business day after the announcement and reaches the series about a day later) is read from the Bank's press releases and reported as announced_change.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `announced_change` | object | The newest scheduled rate decision from the Bank's press releases when it moves the rate and series V39079 has not yet published its effective date (checked when the wanted date is after the latest observation and within 14 days of today); null otherwise, including once the series has caught up. |
| `as_of` | string |  |
| `attribution` | string | Required attribution under the Bank of Canada terms of use. |
| `changes` | object[] | Rate changes within the history window, newest first, dated the day they took effect (the business day after the announcement); an announced_change in effect is included first. Empty when the rate did not move. |
| `history` | object |  |
| `label` | string |  |
| `last_change` | object | Most recent change within the history window, including an announced_change in effect; null when the rate did not move in it. |
| `note` | string |  |
| `observation_date` | string | Latest business day of series V39079 on or before as_of. When announced_change is in effect, the rate comes from the announcement and this is the last day the series had published. |
| `observed_at_ms` | number |  |
| `rate_percent` | number | Policy rate in percent in effect on as_of: the latest observation on or before it, or the rate set by an announced_change already in effect that the series has not yet published. |
| `series` | string |  |
| `source_url` | string | The Bank of Canada URL that answered (the first page for multi-page scans). |
| `terms_url` | string |  |
| `unit` | string |  |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

post.description: Use for who is buying whom, at what price, and whether the deal is pending or closed. For the coverage and commentary around a deal use news/search.

parameters[tickers].description: Comma-separated ticker symbols, maximum 50. Set this when the caller asks whether a named company is acquiring or being acquired.

parameters[date].description: A single date, YYYY-MM-DD, as shorthand when date_from and date_to would be the same. Leave unset to get the latest deals.

parameters[date_from].description: Earliest date, YYYY-MM-DD, interpreted against date_sort.

parameters[date_to].description: Latest date, YYYY-MM-DD, interpreted against date_sort.

parameters[date_sort].description:
Which deal date to sort on. Use announced for a chronology of new deals, expected for pending closes, or completed for deals that have closed.

Provider reference: allowed values ["expected", "completed", "announced"].

parameters[importance].description:
Minimum importance level, matched as greater than or equal to the value given. Raise it when the caller only wants large or notable deals.

Provider reference: allowed values ["0", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5"].

parameters[updated].description: Unix timestamp in UTC; returns only records updated at or after it. Set this when polling for changes since a previous call.

page.description:
Zero-based page offset, capped at 100000. Prefer narrowing by date over paging deep.

Provider reference: maximum 100000; default 0.

pagesize.description:
Number of records to return, limit 1000.

Provider reference: maximum 1000.

For a subject rather than a company, pass topics with topic_group_by and (for example license agreement,upfront payment) plus dateFrom and dateTo, and displayOutput full to quote the terms. post.description: Start here to find trademark records and their st13 identifiers; pass an st13 to get_trademark for the full record.

brand_name_strategy.description:
How the brand name is matched: Simple = embedded (the site's default), Fuzzy, Phonetic, Stemming, Terms = exact phrase.

Provider reference: allowed values ["Simple", "Fuzzy", "Phonetic", "Stemming", "Terms"]; default "Simple".

cursor.description: Offset of the next page as returned in `next_cursor`; omit for the first page. Pattern: ^[0-9]{1,7}$.

goods_services.description: Goods and services text (brick `goodsServices`).

include_facets.description: Also return aggregate counts (owner, applicant country, office, designation, Nice class, status, mark feature, kind, type) for the whole result set. Adds ~400 KB upstream; request it once, not on every page.

nice_classes.description: Nice classes the record must all carry (brick `niceClass`, all_of).

number.description: Application or registration number as the office writes it (brick `number`, either field).

offices.description: IP office codes, any of (brick `office`): ISO country codes plus EM (EUIPO), WO (Madrid). get_coverage lists every office.

rows.description:
Hits per page (the site uses 30; 60 is its maximum).

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 60; default 30.

sort.description:
Sort order; `score desc` is relevance.

Provider reference: allowed values ["score desc", "applicationDate desc", "applicationDate asc"]; default "score desc".

200.description:
Search trademark records in the WIPO Global Brand Database (POST /search). Combine a brand name (embedded, fuzzy, phonetic, stemming or exact-phrase match), an owner name, an application or registration number, goods and services text, Nice classes, IP offices, designated territories and statuses; all given criteria are ANDed. Pages of up to 60 hits with offset pagination; `include_facets` adds the aggregate counts the site's Explore view shows (owner, country, class, status...).

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `results` as the primary payload key.

| `application_date` | string | YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `application_number` | string |  |
| `brand_names` | string[] | Verbal elements of the mark as indexed (may repeat per language). |
| `collection` | string | Source collection id (office code + tm), used in image paths. |
| `designations` | string[] |  |
| `expiry_date` | string |  |
| `kind` | string[] |  |
| `logo_ids` | string[] |  |
| `mark_feature` | string | Word, Figurative, Combined, ... |
| `nice_classes` | number[] |  |
| `office` | string | IP office code (EM = EUIPO, WO = Madrid). |
| `record_url` | string | The record in the site's UI. |
| `registration_date` | string |  |
| `registration_number` | string |  |
| `score` | number |  |
| `st13` | string | WIPO ST.13 record identifier; input of get_trademark. |
| `status` | string |  |
| `termination_date` | string |  |
| `thumbnail_urls` | string[] | images.branddb.wipo.int thumbnail per logo id. The image host requires the same HashSearch request header as the API (any GUID); a bare GET answers 403. |
| `type` | string | TRADEMARK, EMBLEM, INN, AO, ... |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

reviews.content:
I absolutely love my 2021 Toyota Camry. From the moment I got it, I honestly fell in love with it. The car looks sporty and modern, but at the same time it’s very comfortable and smooth to drive. It feels reliable and safe, which gives me a lot of confidence, especially as someone still getting used to driving more often.

The fuel efficiency is great, and the interior is clean and well-designed. Everything feels solid and easy to use. It’s definitely a great value for the price. If I had to mention something, I wish it had push-button start, but overall I’m extremely happy with my purchase.

I would definitely recommend this car to anyone looking for something reliable, stylish, and comfortable.
reviews.title: Review

reviews.author: Nasir M
reviews.content: Great value. Car runs great and really smooth. No problems
reviews.title: Review

reviews.author: Mary A
reviews.content:
I absolutely love the features of my car. The push start, sunroof, heated seats, heated steering wheel, and Apple CarPlay are all fantastic. For the value, the car is a great choice. Being a Toyota, its built to last and is also very fuel-efficient. Both the exterior and interior are incredibly clean, which adds to its appeal.

That said, there are a couple of things I wish were different. I’d love if the car had memory seats, and the display screen could be a bit more modern, especially compared to the ones in the Toyota Highlanders. Another small inconvenience is that, unlike the Highlanders where Apple CarPlay connects wirelessly through Bluetooth, my car requires the phone to be plugged in for CarPlay to work. While this isnt a huge issue, it would be more convenient if it were wireless like in the Highlanders.

Overall, it’s a really cute car and an amazing choice for a first car. Im really happy with it!
reviews.title: Review

reviews.author: Amy W
reviews.content: This car runs good, doesn't burn oil and is excellent on fuel. This car is a 4 cylinder and I have kept it up throughout the last three years I've owned it. I replaced some things such as struts, starter, fixed exhaust that leaked and cylinders. Oil change every month and today as a matter of fact, I just had it done. The tires are one year old and the auto shop said that there is a slight leak within the radiator, but that's about it.
reviews.title: Review

reviews.author: Moises M
reviews.content: Good value for a new car considering used prices are a bit crazy right now. Ride is smooth , absorbs bumps and harsh roads are not a problem for this car. I average  about 60 miles to and from work everyday and so far I average  52 mpg, most of it is highway miles too.  10/10 would recommend it to anyone.
reviews.title: Review

post.description: Finding used vehicles for sale near a US ZIP code, comparing prices against CarGurus' market value, or enumerating trims and counts for a model in an area. Chain listing_id into get_listing, entity_id into model_owner_reviews, and use suggest_vehicles or list_makes/list_models to obtain entity ids first.

body_type_group_ids.description: Body style group ids: 0 Coupe, 1 Convertible, 3 Hatchback, 4 Minivan, 5 Pickup Truck, 6 Sedan, 7 SUV / Crossover, 8 Van, 9 Wagon (the numeric part of a listing's body_type_group_id bg<n>).

distance_miles.description:
Search radius in miles; the site offers 10, 25, 50, 75, 100, 150, 200, 500 and 50000 (nationwide). Default 50. Only listings physically within the radius are returned (the site's nationwide store-transfer / home-delivery padding is switched off).

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 50000.

end_year.description:
Latest model year.

Provider reference: minimum 1900; maximum 2100.

entity_id.description: CarGurus ontology id to search: a make (m7 = Toyota), model (d292 = Toyota Camry), model year (c33246) or trim (t56819), from suggest_vehicles, list_makes or list_models. Omit to search all vehicles. Pattern: ^[mdct][0-9]{1,9}$.

make_model_trim_paths.description: Make/model/trim paths as the site encodes them, e.g. ["m7", "m7/d292"] or ["m7/d292/XLE AWD"] (a trims facet value). Usually unnecessary: the site derives them from entity_id.

max_mileage.description:
Maximum odometer miles.

Provider reference: minimum 0.

max_price.description:
Maximum listing price in USD.

Provider reference: minimum 0.

max_results.description:
Return only the first N listings of the page (the site's page is 24 tiles; next_page still advances by site page). Default: the whole page.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 24.

min_mileage.description:
Minimum odometer miles.

Provider reference: minimum 0.

min_price.description:
Minimum listing price in USD.

Provider reference: minimum 0.

page.description:
1-based page number (page 1 carries 18 organic results, later pages 21, plus sponsored tiles); use next_page from the previous result. A page past the last one is invalid_input.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 10000.

sort_dir.description:
Sort direction. Default ASC.

Provider reference: allowed values ["ASC", "DESC"].

sort_type.description:
Sort key: BEST_MATCH (default), DEAL_SCORE (best deals first), PRICE, MILEAGE, PROXIMITY, NEWEST_CAR_YEAR, AGE_IN_DAYS (listing age).

Provider reference: allowed values ["BEST_MATCH", "DEAL_SCORE", "PRICE", "MILEAGE", "PROXIMITY", "NEWEST_CAR_YEAR", "AGE_IN_DAYS"].

start_year.description:
Earliest model year.

Provider reference: minimum 1900; maximum 2100.

zip.description: 5-digit US ZIP code the search radius is centred on. A ZIP the site cannot resolve is invalid_input. Pattern: ^[0-9]{5}$.

200.description:
Search CarGurus used-car listings within distance_miles of a US ZIP code. Narrow by ontology entity (make m<n>, model d<n>, trim t<n>) or make_model_trim_paths, price, model year, mileage, body style, transmission and sort order. Returns one page of up to 24 listings (18 on page 1) (id, VIN, title, year/make/model/trim, price in USD with CarGurus' expected price and deal rating, mileage, days on market, distance, colors, powertrain, photo, dealer summary), the total match count, the resolved search location, selected facets with counts (body style, condition, deal rating, transmission, fuel, drivetrain, seller type, color, trims) and the next page number. Sponsored tiles (priority, featured, highlight) are listings marked sponsored=true; a sponsored tile that repeats an organic row on the same page is dropped, as are merchandising cards. Only listings within distance_miles are returned (no nationwide delivery or store-transfer padding).

The response contains the tool result directly.

200.description:
Every vessel of one segment (getVesselSummary with Flag and Service, plus BuildYear when given), sorted by VesselId and paged by offset (page_size default 1000, max 5000). Each page re-fetches the segment and compares the SHA-256 of its sorted VesselId list with the one pinned in the cursor; a mismatch fails with invalid_input issue code publication_changed. A segment over the 32 MiB response cap fails with segment_too_large: split it by build_year. Records are summary rows; records_get returns particulars, dimensions, tonnage, documents and cases.

The response contains the tool result directly.

items.abstract: The present invention relates to the use of an I h chanel modular in the manufacture of a medicament for use in psychiatry. To certain novel methanamine derivatives, to processes for their preparation, to pharmaceutical formulations containing them and to their use in medical therapy, particularly for use in psychiatry.
items.title: MODULATEURS DE CANAL I h?

items.abstract: At least some embodiments of the disclosure include a method and device for information identification. In the method, a base station acquires a notification message about a start of a traffic information service, wherein the notification message carries a traffic information identifier and a timestamp, the traffic information identifier is a service identifier for indicating traffic information, and the timestamp indicates a time point when the base station sends Multicast Channel Scheduling Information (MSI); and the base station sends the MSI according to the notification message, wherein the MSI is indicative of position information and expansion information of a sub-frame where a Multicast Traffic Chanel (MTCH) corresponding to the traffic information is. With the technical solution provided in the disclosure, the power consumption for an On Board Unit (OBU) to acquire traffic and scheduling information is further reduced, and it is realized that the OBU receives the required traffic information timely.
items.title: PROCÉDÉ ET DISPOSITIF POUR IDENTIFICATION D'INFORMATIONS

items.abstract: The facility is of the type that has a pair of side bars (1,1) acting as inclined supports for an upper sheet (2) with openings (8) for inserting the plants, a closed lower sheet (4) acting as a collector, and at least one intermdiate sheet (3) with openings determining a cascade trajectory for the water with the nutrients. The invention consist in providing a multi-layer uppersheet (2) comprising preferably four layers (2a,2b and 2d), which together define narrow Channels (7) for selective use, such that at the time of insertion, the root of each plant is placed in a chanel (7) different from that used by adjacent plants. Furthermore according to the invention, the openings (8) for the insertion of the plants form two marginal and longitudinal lines. In this way, the roots of the adjacent plants can be completely isolated during the first growth phase thereof, preventing interference therebetween and allowing plants with different growth rates and even different types of plants to be arranged on the facility, generating, in turn, continuous production and an improved yield from the facility.

privacy_policies.description: The Microsoft Data Privacy Notice describes the collection and use of personal employment data of employees, external staff, candidates and guests. The Notice is available to employees on Microsoft internal and publicly viewable websites, systems, tools and applications used by employees, external staff, candidates, and guests to enter, edit or view their personal data. For description of Data Privacy Framework, please see the section "Where we store and process personal data”: https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?Linkid=518021
privacy_policies.name: Microsoft Data Privacy Notice

value.purpose:
Microsoft collects data from Microsoft product users and employees, external staff, candidates and guests through interactions with them and through their interactions with Microsoft products, in accordance with the Microsoft Privacy Statement (for Microsoft product users) and the Microsoft Global Data Privacy Notice for Employees, External Staff, Candidates and Guests. The personal data we process related to product users is provided by data subjects directly, and we get some of it by collecting data about interactions, use, and experiences with our products. The data we collect depends on the context of interactions with Microsoft and the choices users make, including privacy settings and the products and features used. We also obtain data about users from third parties. Microsoft uses the data we collect to provide rich, interactive experiences. In particular, we use data to provide our products, which includes updating, securing, and troubleshooting, as well as providing support.
 
Microsoft processes data to improve and develop our products, personalize our products and make recommendations, and advertise and market to users, which includes sending promotional communications, targeting advertising, and presenting relevant offers. We also use the data to operate our business, which includes analyzing our performance, meeting our legal obligations, developing our workforce and doing research. The personal data Microsoft processes related to employees, external staff, candidates and guests is processed to administer the employment contract, offer letter or other commitments we have made to the individual, and for other overriding and legitimate business purposes, legally required purposes, and other uses where permissible and in accordance with applicable laws and consultation requirements, as further detailed in the Microsoft Global Data Privacy Notice for Employees, External Staff, Candidates and Guests.
 
Microsoft data processing also includes sharing data, when it is required to provide the service or carry out the transactions requested. We share personal data with consent or to complete any transaction or provide any product data subjects have requested or authorized. We also share data with Microsoft-controlled affiliates and subsidiaries; with vendors working on our behalf; when required by law or to respond to legal process; to protect our customers; to protect lives; to maintain the security of our products; and to protect the rights and property of Microsoft and its customers. All U.S. subsidiaries using the Microsoft brand name are covered entities, as well as those subsidiaries listed above, which use different names. Certain Microsoft U.S. entities continue to maintain their own DPF certification, including LinkedIn Corporation and GitHub.

frameworks.description: Framework ids: 1 = EU-U.S. DPF, 2 = Swiss-U.S. DPF, 3 = UK Extension to the EU-U.S. DPF.

industry_ids.description: Industry row ids from list_reference_data(kind=industries). Several ids share one industry name; pass every id you want to match.

page.description:

page_size.description:

query.description: Text matched against the organization's public display name (substring, case-insensitive on the site). Omit for the full list.

start_letter.description: Only organizations whose display name starts with this letter or digit. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9]$.

states.description: Two-letter U.S. state or territory codes (e.g. CA, NY, DC, PR).

status.description:

statutory_bodies.description: The U.S. statutory body with jurisdiction over the participant.

verification_method.description:

Provider reference: allowed values ["Self-Assessment", "Outside Compliance Review"].

post.description: Find US stores near a postal code or city and state, nearest first with the distance in miles. Returns the fixed nearest set Domino's publishes for the query (at most 10 stores) in one complete response; the store lookup has no page, limit, cursor or radius parameter upstream, so this is not paginated and nothing beyond that set is reachable for one query.

service_method.description:
CARRYOUT (default) returns the nearest stores for the postal code or city and state; each store reports availability.delivery. Domino's answers a DELIVERY store search only for a full street address, which this function does not take, so DELIVERY fails with invalid_input (street_address_required) rather than an upstream error.

Provider reference: allowed values ["CARRYOUT", "DELIVERY"]; default "CARRYOUT".

post.description: Official ECB EUR exchange rates (e.g. EUR/USD reference rate on a date, latest EUR/JPY, a month of EUR/GBP), or a cross rate such as USD/JPY computed from ECB reference rates.

base.description: With quote: also derive the cross rate quote-per-base (e.g. base USD, quote JPY gives JPY per 1 USD) from the two EUR legs on each common date. Non-EUR. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z]{3}$.

currencies.description: ISO 4217 codes of the currencies to quote against the euro, e.g. ["USD", "JPY", "GBP"]. Case-insensitive. EUR itself is not a series (every rate is per 1 EUR). Optional when base/quote is given.

date.description: One day, YYYY-MM-DD. Weekends and TARGET holidays have no rates (not_found). Mutually exclusive with start_date/end_date. Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

end_date.description: Last day of a range, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

quote.description: With base: the currency the cross rate is expressed in. Non-EUR, different from base. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z]{3}$.

start_date.description: First day of a range, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

200.description:
Euro foreign exchange reference rates from the ECB (EXR dataflow, series D.{CUR}.EUR.SP00.A): units of each currency per 1 EUR for the latest business day (default), one date or a date range, each row with its actual observation date. 200.description:
Player box score (player stats, props auditing) for one game from ESPN's `site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/{sport}/{league}/summary?event=`: the event card (status, final score), per-team per-period linescores, and every player's stat line grouped by ESPN's categories with ESPN's stat keys, labels and descriptions preserved: NFL passing/rushing/receiving/defensive/kicking/punting/returns, NHL forwards/defense and goalies (shots on goal = key `shotsTotal`, time on ice, saves, save percentage), NBA points/rebounds/assists/minutes, MLB batting and pitching, soccer match rosters including goalkeepers (saves, goals conceded). Categories are read generically, so any league ESPN gives a box score for works. Also the per-team game leaders (e.g. passing/rushing/receiving yards, goals/assists/points). A scheduled game has no player lines (`teams: []` with a `note`); when ESPN reports every player stat as 0 for a match with a non-zero score (some women's soccer competitions) the lines are null with a `note` rather than zeros. An unknown event, or an event of another league, is `not_found`.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `teams` as the primary payload key.

status.description: Only players with this status, matched case- and punctuation-insensitively against the status, its abbreviation and its code: e.g. Out, day-to-day, DD, Questionable, IR.

team.description: Only these teams: one or more ESPN team ids (e.g. 29) or abbreviations (e.g. CBJ, LAL), comma-separated, from `teams`. Every named team is returned, with an empty list when ESPN lists no injuries for it. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9]{1,10}(\s*,\s*[A-Za-z0-9]{1,10}){0,39}$.

200.description:
NFL, NBA, WNBA, MLB, NHL and college football injury report (who is out, injured reserve, day-to-day, questionable) from `site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/{sport}/{league}/injuries` (one keyless request): every team ESPN lists with its injured players, each with athlete_id, name, position, status (Out, Day-To-Day, Questionable, Injured Reserve, IL...), note date, short and long comment, injury type and details when ESPN gives them, and the ESPN player URL, plus the feed timestamp. ESPN omits teams with no injuries from the report (e.g. NHL: 31 of 32 clubs listed), so pass `team` (one or more ESPN team ids or abbreviations, comma-separated, e.g. `MIN,CAR,CBJ` for tonight's clubs): each named team is always returned, a healthy one with an empty list, `count: 0` and a note (one extra request resolves the names against the league's team list; an unknown team is `not_found`). `status` filters players. Verified for basketball/nba, basketball/wnba, football/nfl, baseball/mlb, hockey/nhl and football/college-football; a league with no listed injuries (offseason, or one ESPN does not report, e.g. soccer) is an empty `teams` list with a `note`. An unknown sport/league, or a league ESPN keeps no injury report for (racing, golf, MMA), is `not_found`.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `teams` as the primary payload key.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `abbreviation` | string | From the league's team list when the team was named in `team`, else from a listed player still on the team; null when every listed player has since moved. |
| `count` | number |  |
| `display_name` | string |  |
| `injuries` | object[] |  |
| `note` | string | Set on a team named in `team` that has no listed (or no status-matching) injuries: ESPN's report omits healthy teams, so this means no reported injuries, not missing data. |
| `slug` | string |  |
| `team_id` | string |  |
| `url` | string | ESPN team clubhouse URL. |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

injuries.long_comment: Gilbert continues to deal with patella tendinitis. His last chance to appear this preseason is Friday against the Mavericks.
injuries.short_comment: Gilbert (knee) won't play in Monday's preseason game against the Thunder, per Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network.

injuries.long_comment: Wiggins and most of Atlanta's regulars won't play in the penultimate preseason game. He finished with 13 points (4-9 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, an assist and two steals across 20 minutes off the bench in Saturday's 119-117 preseason win over the Pacers.
injuries.short_comment: Wiggins (rest) won't play in Monday's preseason game against the Thunder, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.

injuries.long_comment: Okongwu is getting the night off Monday with Atlanta resting a number of starters. His next chance to play arrives Friday against Dallas.
injuries.short_comment: Okongwu (rest) is out for Monday's preseason game against the Thunder, per Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network.

injuries.long_comment: McCollum and most of Atlanta's regulars won't play in the penultimate preseason game. He recorded 12 points (2-4 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 7-7 FT) and five rebounds across 19 minutes in Saturday's 119-117 preseason win over the Pacers.
injuries.short_comment: McCollum (rest) won't play in Monday's preseason game against the Thunder, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.

injuries.long_comment: Dort is sitting out Monday for maintenance purposes. The veteran swingman's next chance to play is Friday against Dallas.
injuries.short_comment: Dort (rest) is out for Monday's preseason game against the Thunder, per Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network.

injuries.long_comment: Johnson and most of Atlanta's regulars won't suit up for the penultimate preseason contest. He tallied 20 points (8-12 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 2-3 FT), seven rebounds and three assists over 25 minutes in Saturday's 119-117 preseason win over the Pacers.
injuries.short_comment: Johnson (rest) won't play in Monday's preseason game against the Thunder, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.

injuries.long_comment: Daniels and most of Atlanta's regulars will rest during the Hawks' penultimate preseason contest. He tallied 13 points (6-16 FG, 1-3 3Pt), 11 rebounds, an assist and a steal across 21 minutes in Thursday's 123-116 preseason win over the Spurs but struggled with his shot against the Pacers on Saturday.
injuries.short_comment: Daniels (rest) has been ruled out for Monday's preseason game against the Thunder, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.

injuries.long_comment: Veesaar suffered the injury during a workout on Sept. 15, and an MRI confirmed the diagnosis. The No. 52 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Veesaar was expected to spend a lot of time with Atlanta's G League affiliate this season.
injuries.short_comment: Veesaar was diagnosed with a torn right ACL and is expected to miss the 2026-27 season, the Hawks announced Monday.

injuries.long_comment: Gueye will be re-evaluated by medical staff in 3-to-4 months, which means he'll miss all of training camp and preseason and likely the start of the 2026-27 regular season. It's a brutal blow for the fourth-year big man, given that the Hawks used the No. 23 overall pick of the 2026 NBA Draft to select St. John's product Zuby Ejiofor. Gueye's absence means Ejiofor will have more opportunities in the preseason, and the rookie could establish a key role off the bench behind Onyeka Okongwu and projected backup center Jock Landale (ankle).
injuries.short_comment: Gueye underwent surgery Tuesday to repair a fractured left foot that he suffered during a workout last week, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.

injuries.long_comment: Garza took an inadvertent elbow to the nose from teammate Chris Cenac, and the former was taken to the locker room shortly thereafter. Assuming Garza doesn't return, he'll end his night with eight points (4-9 FG), seven rebounds and one assist over 11 minutes.
injuries.short_comment: Garza (nose) went to the locker room late in the fourth quarter of Saturday's preseason game against the 76ers, Bobby Manning of CLNS Media Network reports.

injuries.long_comment: Carter played 25 minutes during Boston's preseason opener against Cleveland on Thursday, but the third-year pro is under the weather and not be available for Saturday's contest. His next chance to play is Wednesday against Charlotte.
injuries.short_comment: Carter (illness) has been ruled out for Saturday's exhibition game against the 76ers, Jack Simone of BostonSportsJournal.com reports.

injuries.long_comment: Harper is working through right shoulder illness, which has prevented him from playing in each of the Celtics' first two preseason games. His next opportunity to play is Wednesday against the Hornets.
injuries.short_comment: Harper (shoulder) has been ruled out for Saturday's preseason game against the 76ers, Jack Simone of BostonSportsJournal.com reports.

injuries.long_comment: Jefferson will be sidelined for his third straight exhibition. The rookie forward will have one more chance to return in the preseason Oct. 14 against the Heat.
injuries.short_comment: Jefferson (back) is out for Monday's preseason game against the Wizards, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.

injuries.long_comment: Brown has yet to suit up during the preseason as he continues to work his way back from a left ankle issue. His final chance to get in an exhibition is Wednesday against the Heat.
injuries.short_comment: Brown (ankle) is out for Monday's preseason game against the Wizards, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.

injuries.long_comment: Anderson will miss a second straight game due to a left ankle sprain. His next chance to suit up will come in Wednesday's exhibition against the Celtics.
injuries.short_comment: Anderson (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's preseason game against Milwaukee.

injuries.long_comment: Allen performed well in the Hornets' opening preseason game, posting 13 points in 14 minutes, but he will miss Sunday's contest with a knee injury. Sion James and Royce O'Neale could see extra action with Allen out of the lineup.
injuries.short_comment: Allen will not play in Sunday's preseason game against the Bucks due to right knee soreness.

injuries.long_comment: It doesn't sound like the two-way guard will be available for the preseason, but he's hopeful to not miss any time during the G League season. Boswell is not expected to be a significant part of the Hornets' rotation this season.
injuries.short_comment: Boswell is rehabbing a right knee injury, and he's hopeful to be cleared for basketball activities prior to the start of the G League season in late October.

injuries.long_comment: White missed time with a left calf strain last season and is now in jeopardy of starting the regular season on the inactive list. If the 26-year-old guard is forced to miss time beyond the preseason, Christian Anderson and Dennis Schroder would likely see increased playing time.
injuries.short_comment: The Hornets announced Monday that White suffered a left calf strain during training camp and will not play during the preseason.

injuries.long_comment: Knueppel's status for Opening Night remains uncertain as he continues to work his way back from his left hamstring injury. Peterson's comments suggest the Hornets aren't ready to rule out the second-year wing, though his availability will likely become clearer as training camp progresses. He has already been ruled out for the entire preseason, to be clear.
injuries.short_comment: Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday that he "doesn't know" whether Knueppel (hamstring) will be available for the team's regular-season opener against the Nets, Owen Watterson of SI.com reports.

injuries.long_comment: Williams will be re-evaluated the first week of the regular season, putting his status for Opening Night in the air. Williams will have a difficult path to minutes this season as he competes with the likes of Naz Reid, Royce O'Neale and Tidjane Salaun.
injuries.short_comment: Williams will miss the preseason after suffering a right hamstring injury, the Hornets announced Friday.

injuries.long_comment: Collins has yet to suit up in the preseason due to a toe injury but is making progress ahead of the regular season. The big man's final chance to suit up in the preseason will come Friday against Minnesota.
injuries.short_comment: Collins (toe) is progressing in his recovery but has been ruled out for Wednesday's preseason meeting with the Bucks, K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network reports.

injuries.long_comment: Awaka banged his knee in Friday's preseason game against Memphis. The undrafted rookie can be deemed questionable for Wednesday's exhibition versus the Bucks.
injuries.short_comment: Awaka (knee) didn't practice Tuesday, per K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network.

injuries.long_comment: It's unclear why Okoro didn't practice, though he can be considered questionable for Wednesday's exhibition against Milwaukee. If the 25-year-old wing is unable to suit up, Leonard Miller, Jordan Hawkins and Buddy Hield could see a bump in playing time.
injuries.short_comment: Okoro (undisclosed) didn't participate in Tuesday's practice, K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network reports.

injuries.long_comment: Sellers continues to deal with lower-back soreness that has limited his preseason availability. The two-way guard will look to return to action as Chicago completes its exhibition schedule, though his immediate fantasy outlook remains limited.
injuries.short_comment: Sellers (back) did not play in Sunday's 133-128 preseason loss to Denver.

injuries.long_comment: This is a huge blow for Claxton and it rules him out for the entire preseason. For now, fantasy managers can consider him questionable for Opening Night on Oct. 21 against the Raptors. Jalen Smith is the next man up on the depth chart for Chicago, followed by Zach Collins (toe).
injuries.short_comment: Claxton tweaked his hamstring and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Chuck Swirsky of the Bulls Radio Network of the Bulls Radio Network reports.

200.description:
One athlete's public profile from `site.web.api.espn.com/apis/common/v3/sports/{sport}/{league}/athletes/{athlete_id}` (identity, position, current team, status, age, birth date/place, height, weight, experience, draft, college, headshot) and, unless `include_statistics` is false, career statistics by season from `.../athletes/{athlete_id}/stats`: ESPN's categories with labels, stat names, display names, per-season rows (team, position, values as ESPN prints them) and career totals. Stat names and units are sport-specific and kept verbatim; a player without a statistics page keeps `statistics: null` with a warning. An unknown athlete_id is `not_found`. ESPN's career statistics endpoint answers 404 for many soccer players (goalkeepers included); then `statistics` is null with `statistics_unavailable_reason`, and `season_summary` carries the bio's current-season headline stats (saves, clean sheets, goals against for a goalkeeper).

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `athlete` | object |  |
| `league` | object |  |
| `observed_at_ms` | number | When this program observed the upstream response (ms since epoch). |
| `season` | object | Season identity as ESPN labels it: `type` is the season-type code (NFL 1 pre, 2 regular, 3 post; soccer competitions use large codes such as 14308). |
| `season_summary` | object | Current-season headline stats from the athlete bio (`statsSummary`), e.g. a goalkeeper's saves, clean sheets and goals against; ESPN fills it for soccer players whose career statistics endpoint answers 404. Null when ESPN sends none. |
| `sport` | string |  |
| `statistics` | object |  |
| `statistics_unavailable_reason` | string | Why `statistics` is null (ESPN has no statistics page for the athlete, or statistics were not requested); null when statistics are present. |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

200.description:
A team's season schedule from `site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/{sport}/{league}/teams/{team_id}/schedule[?season=&seasontype=]`, as a bounded window (`offset`/`limit`, default 50) over the full list with `next_offset` continuation: every event with UTC start, status (including STATUS_POSTPONED), venue, competitors and final scores. Without `season` ESPN returns the current season. `season` is checked against ESPN's `requestedSeason` echo (the season the events belong to), not the top-level current season, so past seasons work (e.g. Manchester United 2024 = 2024-25); a season ESPN answers with a different season is `not_found`, and a non-current season carries a `not_current_season` warning naming ESPN's label (NHL/NBA seasons are labelled by their end year, so the 2026-27 NHL season is 2027). For soccer ESPN splits the season into completed results and upcoming fixtures (`fixture=true`); the program fetches both (fixtures only for the current or a future season, since ESPN's fixture list ignores `season`) and returns one chronological list, so a competition whose season has not started yet lists its fixtures instead of nothing. A soccer `league` is one competition; `league: "all"` (ESPN's All Competitions view) spans every competition the club or national team plays, with each event's competition in its `season.name`. An unknown team_id is `not_found`.

schema.description:
A team's season schedule from `site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/{sport}/{league}/teams/{team_id}/schedule[?season=&seasontype=]`, as a bounded window (`offset`/`limit`, default 50) over the full list with `next_offset` continuation: every event with UTC start, status (including STATUS_POSTPONED), venue, competitors and final scores. Without `season` ESPN returns the current season. `season` is checked against ESPN's `requestedSeason` echo (the season the events belong to), not the top-level current season, so past seasons work (e.g. Manchester United 2024 = 2024-25); a season ESPN answers with a different season is `not_found`, and a non-current season carries a `not_current_season` warning naming ESPN's label (NHL/NBA seasons are labelled by their end year, so the 2026-27 NHL season is 2027). For soccer ESPN splits the season into completed results and upcoming fixtures (`fixture=true`); the program fetches both (fixtures only for the current or a future season, since ESPN's fixture list ignores `season`) and returns one chronological list, so a competition whose season has not started yet lists its fixtures instead of nothing. A soccer `league` is one competition; `league: "all"` (ESPN's All Competitions view) spans every competition the club or national team plays, with each event's competition in its `season.name`. An unknown team_id is `not_found`.

200.description:
One page of rounds under `data`, with `next_cursor` beside it (null on the last page). When a name matched nothing, `did_you_mean` lists up to three near names (`id`, `name`) to retry with. Each round is what Fireround checked: the company, stage, money, valuation when stated, date, certainty, investors, the sentence that states it and the pages it was read from.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `data` as the primary payload key.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Stable round id, company_key:stage:announced_on. |
| `url` | string | The round's company page on fireround.dev, with every source and the evidence for each field. |
| `company` | object | name, domain, website, description, sector, headquarters. |
| `stage` | string | One of pre_seed, seed, pre_a, series_a, series_b, series_c, series_d_plus, growth, bridge, debt, grant, convertible, secondary, undisclosed, other. |
| `stage_as_written` | string | The stage as the source wrote it, for example `Series B-2`. |
| `amount` | object | usd_millions (null when undisclosed or unconvertible), as_written, currency. |
| `valuation` | string | The post- or pre-money valuation as written, when a source states it. |
| `valuation_disclosed` | boolean | true when a valuation is stated; false when a source says outright that it was not disclosed; null when no source says either way. A null valuation with false here is a known non-disclosure, not a gap. |
| `total_as_written` | string | A larger figure stated beside the round, such as funding to date or the whole financing; never the round's own amount. |
| `announced_on` | string | YYYY-MM-DD; read with date_precision (day, week, month, unknown). |
| `date_precision` | string |  |
| `certainty` | string | announced (closed on the record), reported (said to have closed, citing unnamed sources), expected (still being raised), or unconfirmed (reported or expected, and never confirmed). |
| `verified` | boolean | True when a model read the round back against its sources and they agreed, with any field it corrected applied. |
| `provisional` | boolean | True when the round is public but carries a recorded doubt (thin evidence, low confidence, or no stated amount); treat it as provisional. |
| `earlier_round` | boolean | True for an earlier round of the company, verified on its own, rather than recent news. |
| `is_extension` | boolean | True for an extension of an earlier round. |
| `lead_investors` | string[] |  |
| `other_investors` | string[] |  |
| `evidence` | string | The sentence from a source that states the round. |
| `primary_source` | object | The round's official announcement: url, and kind (company for the company's own page, wire for its newswire release). Null when the sources hold neither. |
| `sources` | object[] | Up to 3 pages the round was read from, in reading order (the official announcement first, then established outlets, then the rest): url, title, publisher, published. |
| `source_count` | number | How many pages the round was read from in all. |
| `trending` | object | While the round is in its first 72 hours: rank, people_on_x, outlets, hn_points. Null after. |
| `previous_rounds` | object[] | The company's other rounds announced before this one, newest first, up to 5: id, stage, stage_as_written, amount (usd_millions, as_written), announced_on, lead_investors, url (the round's official announcement when it has one). |

stage.description: Comma-separated stages, any of: pre_seed, seed, pre_a, series_a, series_b, series_c, series_d_plus, growth, bridge, debt, grant, convertible, secondary, undisclosed, other, or the words for them. For example `series_a,series_b` or `Series A`.

certainty.description:
Only rounds of this certainty: announced (closed on the record), reported (said to have closed by a publisher citing unnamed sources), expected (still being raised), unconfirmed. Absent means every certainty but unconfirmed.

Provider reference: allowed values ["announced", "reported", "expected", "unconfirmed"].

sector.description: The company's sector, as fireround classifies it: ai, ai infrastructure, developer tools, data and analytics, cybersecurity, enterprise software, fintech, payments, insurtech, crypto, healthtech, biotech, medtech, climate, energy, mobility, robotics, hardware, semiconductors, quantum, space, defense, consumer, ecommerce, marketplace, media and gaming, edtech, hr tech, legal tech, proptech, logistics, agtech and food, manufacturing, other. Case and dashes don't matter and common other names work (`ai-infra`, `healthcare`, `dev tools`). A broad sector takes in its narrower ones, so one call covers them: `ai` includes ai infrastructure; `fintech` includes payments, insurtech and crypto; `climate` includes energy. The narrower word alone reads only that sector.

limit.description:
Rounds per page, 1 to 50. Defaults to 20. Each round is a full record of about 1,500 characters, so read more with `cursor` rather than a larger page.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 50.

cursor.description: The `next_cursor` of the previous page, to read the next one under the same filters.

builds.how_to_play: Charge in, use Bloodrage, and keep Battle Shout up. Between Charge and Anger Management's trickle you rarely start a fight with an empty bar, so you can Rend straight away on anything that will live a while. Press Overpower every time the target dodges and put spare Rage into Heroic Strike. You learn Slam and Cleave at 20: Slam hits hard, but its 1.5 sec cast delays your next swing, so start it right after a swing lands. If a pull goes wrong, Tactical Mastery (level 14) keeps up to 10 Rage when you drop into Defensive Stance, and Improved Tactical Mastery keeps up to 15 more.
builds.name: Two-hander leveling with Anger Management
builds.summary: A two-handed leveling build that heads straight for Anger Management, which in Forever generates Rage in combat as well as slowing Rage loss. Improved Heroic Strike at 3/3 takes 3 Rage off your Rage dump, and 2 points of Deflection add a little parry.

talents.name: Improved Heroic Strike
talents.reason: Rank 3 cuts Heroic Strike's cost by 3 Rage (1 per rank), and Heroic Strike is where most of your spare Rage goes, so the saving adds up over every fight.

talents.name: Deflection
talents.reason: Rank 2 adds 2% Parry chance (1% per rank); every parry is a hit you don't take while you solo, and these 2 points complete the 5 tier 1 points that open tier 2.

talents.name: Improved Tactical Mastery
talents.reason: At 5/5 Tactical Mastery keeps up to an additional 15 Rage when you change stances, so a switch to Defensive Stance on a bad pull costs you little; 5 points here are required for Anger Management.

talents.name: Anger Management
talents.reason: Generates 1 Rage every 3 sec in combat and reduces Rage loss out of combat by 30%, so you start and finish fights with Rage to spend.

builds.how_to_play: Let the tank get a few hits in first; Heroic Strike causes a high amount of threat, so hold it until the tank has a lead. Rend the tank's target on anything bigger than a trash mob, Overpower whenever it dodges, and Slam right after a swing when Slam is off cooldown. When two enemies stand together and nothing crowd-controlled is nearby, use Cleave instead of Heroic Strike. Anger Management keeps Rage coming even when you aren't taking hits, which is exactly the situation in a group.
builds.name: Anger Management with Improved Rend
builds.summary: For dungeon runs at 20: the same Anger Management core, but with 3 points in Improved Rend, which makes Rend's bleed 35% stronger, since enemies live longer when someone else tanks. Those 3 points also unlock Deep Wounds for your next point at level 21.

talents.name: Improved Rend
talents.reason: Rank 3 adds 35% to Rend's bleed damage (12% at rank 1, 23% at rank 2), and 3 points here unlock Deep Wounds.

talents.name: Improved Heroic Strike
talents.reason: Rank 2 cuts Heroic Strike's cost by 2 Rage, and with Improved Rend's 3 points it makes the 5 tier 1 points that open tier 2.

talents.name: Improved Tactical Mastery
talents.reason: At 5/5 Tactical Mastery keeps up to an additional 15 Rage when you change stances, so a switch to Defensive Stance on a bad pull costs you little; 5 points here are required for Anger Management.

talents.name: Anger Management
talents.reason: Generates 1 Rage every 3 sec in combat and reduces Rage loss out of combat by 30%, so you start and finish fights with Rage to spend.

builds.how_to_play: Open with Charge while you are still out of combat, then Hamstring at once so the target can't walk out of melee range. Use Bloodrage after Charge, never before: it puts you in combat, and Charge can't be used in combat. Rend the target, press Overpower whenever they dodge, and spend spare Rage on Heroic Strike. Slam has a cast time, so use it only when the target stands and fights you. Disarm needs Defensive Stance: use it on Rogues, Warriors, Paladins and Shamans when they start hitting hard. Against several melee players, Thunder Clap makes them attack slower and Retaliation punishes every hit they land from the front. When you are losing, change to Defensive Stance; Tactical Mastery and Improved Tactical Mastery mean you keep Rage when you do.
builds.name: Deflection and Anger Management for PvP
builds.summary: A level 20 PvP build that spends on Rage and survival instead of Improved Rend. Five points of Deflection add 5% parry against melee classes, and Anger Management keeps Rage coming while casters and Hunters keep you at range. Compared with the dungeon build you give up Improved Rend and the path to Deep Wounds, which pay off on long fights against a target that stands still, not against players who move and heal. Improved Charge and Improved Overpower come at 30.

talents.name: Deflection
talents.reason: At 5/5 you parry 5% more often (1% per rank). Rogues, Warriors, Paladins and Shamans all fight you in melee, every parried swing is damage you don't take, and 5 points here open tier 2.

talents.name: Improved Tactical Mastery
talents.reason: At 5/5 Tactical Mastery keeps up to an additional 15 Rage when you change stances, so you can drop into Defensive Stance under pressure and come back without an empty bar; 5 points here are required for Anger Management.

talents.name: Anger Management
talents.reason: Generates 1 Rage every 3 sec while in combat, so you still build Rage while a Mage or Hunter keeps you from hitting them, and reduces Rage loss out of combat by 30%, so you often start the next fight with Rage left.

summary.text: This gene encodes a tumor suppressor protein containing transcriptional activation, DNA binding, and oligomerization domains. The encoded protein responds to diverse cellular stresses to regulate expression of target genes, thereby inducing cell cycle arrest, apoptosis, senescence, DNA repair, or changes in metabolism. Mutations in this gene are associated with a variety of human cancers, including hereditary cancers such as Li-Fraumeni syndrome. Alternative splicing of this gene and the use of alternate promoters result in multiple transcript variants and isoforms. Additional isoforms have also been shown to result from the use of alternate translation initiation codons from identical transcript variants (PMIDs: 12032546, 20937277). [provided by RefSeq, Dec 2016]

Orthologs of one gene from NCBI's ortholog sets: give the gene as for `get` (`gene_id`, `symbol` with `organism`, or `url`) and optionally `taxa` (taxonomy IDs or names at any rank: `mouse`, `Danio rerio`, `rodents`) to keep only those organisms. Each ortholog is a gene row with GeneID, symbol, organism, location and cross-references, in NCBI's order; the set pages with `limit` and `offset`. A gene without orthologs, or none in the taxa, returns an empty list.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `orthologs` as the primary payload key.

| `current_gene_id` | string | For a `replaced` record, the GeneID that replaced it; otherwise null. |
| `ensembl_gene_ids` | string[] | Ensembl gene IDs, e.g. `ENSG00000141510`. |

| `nomenclature` | object | The official nomenclature record: authority and its ID (HGNC:11998 for human, MGI:98834 for mouse, ZFIN, RGD, FlyBase, EcoCyc...). Null when no authority names the gene. |
| `omim_ids` | string[] | OMIM gene entry numbers (human genes), e.g. `191170`. |
| `organism` | object | The organism the gene belongs to. |
| `source_url` | string | The gene's page on NCBI Gene, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/<gene_id>, for attribution and follow-up. |
| `status` | string | `live` for current records; `replaced` and `discontinued` appear only with `include_discontinued`. |
| `symbol` | string | Official gene symbol, e.g. `TP53` (human), `Trp53` (mouse), `tp53` (zebrafish); `LOC` symbols for genes without an official name. |

| `uniprot_ids` | string[] | Reviewed UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot accessions of the encoded proteins, e.g. `P04637`; pass to uniprot-org. |

condition.description:

make.description: Make names as the site spells them (facet make), e.g. ['Toyota'].

odometer_max.description:
Mileage bounds in miles, inclusive.

Provider reference: minimum 0.

price_max.description:
Internet price bounds in whole US dollars, inclusive.

Provider reference: minimum 0.

radius_miles.description:
Search radius in miles around zip (geoRadius); needs zip. The site's own menu offers 5, 25, 50, 100, 200, 250, 500 and 1000.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 5000.

sort.description:
Sort order, passed to the site as its own sort expression (e.g. internetPrice asc). The site's store/make boost order can still interleave rows; without sort the site's default order applies.

year_max.description:
Model-year bounds, inclusive; sent as the list of years in the range (the API rejects a min-max year range).

Provider reference: minimum 1980; maximum 2100.

zip.description: US ZIP code to measure distance from (geoZip). Alone it only fills distance_miles (every match nationwide is kept); with radius_miles it restricts the search. Without it distance_miles is null. Pattern: ^[0-9]{5}$.
